claims.claim: Cobb notes Crispin's surviving second mosaic is on a smaller scale and more obliquely expressed, the novel implying that is why it lasts.
claims.source: Christopher Cobb, 'Guy Gavriel Kay and the Psychology of History', Foundation (Summer 2005), reprinted on Bright Weavings
claims.quote: on a smaller scale and more obliquely expressed

claims.claim: Cobb contrasts Kay's sense of proportion, the smallness of the human being in relation to the world, with Silverberg's hero who masters history.
claims.source: Christopher Cobb, 'Guy Gavriel Kay and the Psychology of History', Foundation (Summer 2005), reprinted on Bright Weavings
claims.quote: the smallness of the human being in relation to the world

claims.claim: Töyrylä estimates about sixty per cent of Tigana is focalized through Devin or Dianora, with at least nineteen other identifiable focal characters and most chapters alternating three or more perspectives.
claims.source: Roosa Töyrylä, 'Ambiguities and Divided Loyalties: Focalization in Guy Gavriel Kay's Tigana' (BA thesis, University of Helsinki, 2017)
claims.quote: About sixty per cent of the text

claims.claim: Töyrylä shows Dianora's passages use free indirect thought with the character's own metaphors, deictics and incomplete sentences, amplifying the emotional notes.
claims.source: Roosa Töyrylä, 'Ambiguities and Divided Loyalties: Focalization in Guy Gavriel Kay's Tigana' (BA thesis, University of Helsinki, 2017)
claims.quote: incomplete sentences point in the direction of the character

claims.claim: Töyrylä points to the long list of verbs ('battered and levelled and burned... and killed... and taken away') as the character's voice inside the narration.
claims.source: Roosa Töyrylä, 'Ambiguities and Divided Loyalties: Focalization in Guy Gavriel Kay's Tigana' (BA thesis, University of Helsinki, 2017)

claims.claim: Töyrylä notes Alberico is a regular focal character, which humanises him with frustration and fear without making him sympathetic.
claims.source: Roosa Töyrylä, 'Ambiguities and Divided Loyalties: Focalization in Guy Gavriel Kay's Tigana' (BA thesis, University of Helsinki, 2017)
claims.quote: Using the antagonist as a focal character makes him

claims.claim: Töyrylä analyses the Ring Dive as narrated twice or thrice through Devin, Dianora and Alessan, with contradictory readings of Brandin's expressionless face.
claims.source: Roosa Töyrylä, 'Ambiguities and Divided Loyalties: Focalization in Guy Gavriel Kay's Tigana' (BA thesis, University of Helsinki, 2017)
claims.quote: some of the events are narrated twice or even thrice

claims.claim: Töyrylä shows Rhun is never a focal character until the final pages, enabling the Valentin twist while other focalizants register him in passing.
claims.source: Roosa Töyrylä, 'Ambiguities and Divided Loyalties: Focalization in Guy Gavriel Kay's Tigana' (BA thesis, University of Helsinki, 2017)
claims.quote: the focalization unexpectedly shifts to him

claims.claim: Töyrylä reads the innkeeper Ettocio: focalized for a few pages, then a shift to narratorial focalization enables the matter-of-fact description of his execution.
claims.source: Roosa Töyrylä, 'Ambiguities and Divided Loyalties: Focalization in Guy Gavriel Kay's Tigana' (BA thesis, University of Helsinki, 2017)
claims.quote: enables the matter-of-fact description of his execution

claims.claim: Töyrylä finds narratorial passages are matter-of-fact description with only minimal commentary (e.g. 'Unfortunately'), denying readers a guiding moral voice.
claims.source: Roosa Töyrylä, 'Ambiguities and Divided Loyalties: Focalization in Guy Gavriel Kay's Tigana' (BA thesis, University of Helsinki, 2017)
claims.quote: matter-of-fact description with only minimal commentary

claims.claim: Töyrylä notes the Senzio courtyard slaughter is narrated in summary with 'according to most reports later' and approximate casualties, the narrator restricting omniscience to what becomes known.
claims.source: Roosa Töyrylä, 'Ambiguities and Divided Loyalties: Focalization in Guy Gavriel Kay's Tigana' (BA thesis, University of Helsinki, 2017)
claims.quote: the narrator is merely reporting what happened, without any commentary

claims.claim: Töyrylä identifies a narrator who reports what the world seems like to an average inhabitant, adopting the Palm's religious stance ('as everyone knows') and using 'word went forth' to mislead truthfully.
claims.source: Roosa Töyrylä, 'Ambiguities and Divided Loyalties: Focalization in Guy Gavriel Kay's Tigana' (BA thesis, University of Helsinki, 2017)
claims.quote: reporting what the world seems like to an average person

claims.claim: Töyrylä analyses tavern-patron and Astibar-town passages focalized through a group, combining sardonic tone with dramatic irony since readers know more.
claims.source: Roosa Töyrylä, 'Ambiguities and Divided Loyalties: Focalization in Guy Gavriel Kay's Tigana' (BA thesis, University of Helsinki, 2017)
claims.quote: a sardonic tone is combined with the deeper level irony

claims.claim: Töyrylä argues Kay's 'outright lie' opening is not a lie: the narrator says only that word went forth of Sandre's death.
claims.source: Roosa Töyrylä, 'Ambiguities and Divided Loyalties: Focalization in Guy Gavriel Kay's Tigana' (BA thesis, University of Helsinki, 2017)
claims.quote: the narrator does not claim that Sandre is dead

claims.feature: authorial aim: ambiguities and divided loyalties
claims.claim: Töyrylä quotes Kay's afterword that Tigana aimed to stretch the reader with ambiguities and divided loyalties in a genre that tends not to work that way.
claims.source: Roosa Töyrylä, 'Ambiguities and Divided Loyalties: Focalization in Guy Gavriel Kay's Tigana' (BA thesis, University of Helsinki, 2017)
claims.quote: to stretch the reader with ambiguities and divided loyalties
